text: Setting clear project goals is essential for success. A useful method is to create SMART goals, which are Specific, Measurable, Achievable, Relevant, and Time-bound. For example, instead of saying "improve the website," you might say "increase user sign-ups by 20% within three months." Once the main goal is set, break it into smaller milestones, such as completing the design phase or finishing user testing. Each milestone should have clear deliverables—the actual outputs, like a report or a prototype, that show progress. Finally, ensure stakeholder alignment by discussing the goals with everyone involved. This helps avoid confusion and makes sure that all team members share the same vision and priorities.
